title: RFI Field Playbook
short_answer: A conflict between contract documents is an RFI, not a field decision. Write it so it gets answered in a day — then work somewhere else while you wait.
summary: A conflict between contract documents is an RFI, not a field decision. Write it so it gets answered in a day — then work somewhere else while you wait.
plain_words: If two sheets disagree, or the partition schedule and the detail disagree, do not pick one and build. That guess becomes our rework. Name both documents, say what each seems to require, propose an answer, and say what it holds up.
when_to_use: Drawings, specs, or schedules conflict and you cannot tell which governs
Before building a guess on a head-of-wall detail, partition type, or finish callout
When the lead or office needs a logged question on commercial jobs
prerequisites: Sheet numbers and detail references for both sides of the conflict
Lead or office path for submitting RFIs on this job

steps.title: Stop the affected work
steps.body: Keep the crew productive on unaffected areas — do not build the guess.

steps.title: Photo
steps.body: Photograph the condition and note sheet and detail numbers.

steps.title: Write the RFI
steps.body: Conflict → what each document appears to require → proposed answer → what is held up.

steps.title: Send through the lead / office path
steps.body: Commercial = logged RFI; residential may start as a call — still get the answer in writing.

steps.title: Do not build while waiting
steps.body: If directed to proceed at risk, that direction comes from the office — document it.

warnings.title: Not a field decision
warnings.body: Precedence between specs and drawings is decided by each project's own precedence clause — read that clause; do not guess which document wins.

experts.tag: Full detail · example that gets answered
experts.summary: "Detail 5/A8.02 shows a slotted deflection track at the corridor head of wall; the partition schedule for type A3 calls for a double slip track. Please confirm which governs. We propose the slotted track per the detail. This holds top track on level 2." "Which head of wall do you want?" sits for a week. The first version answers itself enough that someone can say yes or no in a day.

quality_checks.prompt: Both conflicting documents named with sheet/detail references
Proposed answer and what work is held up are stated
Affected scope stopped — crew not building the guess

common_mistakes.title: Vague one-liner
common_mistakes.wrong: Ask "which head of wall do you want?" with no context
common_mistakes.right: Name both sources, state the conflict, propose an answer, name what is blocked
common_mistakes.why: Vague RFIs sit unanswered; specific ones get a yes or no in a day

common_mistakes.title: Building the guess
common_mistakes.wrong: Pick the detail that looks right and keep framing
common_mistakes.right: Stop affected work; mobilize elsewhere until written answer
common_mistakes.why: Wrong guess becomes our rework at our cost

next_steps.why: If the answer changes scope or price, the CO path still applies
